# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield (formerly Empire)
Appeals Department — [appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Sawyer Delgado
Member ID: W188500611
[My address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-13 — Reference number POC-C3B5D8F398-85355**
**Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Ordering surgeon:** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
**Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon) — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/4827/pdf-Spine-Surgery-2024-10-20.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the lumbar decompression surgery (CPT 63030) that my surgeon requested for me. The notice dated 2026-08-13 states that the request was denied because the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider and approve this service.

I am writing because, when I read the plan's own guideline alongside my medical records, the records appear to meet the criteria the guideline sets out — including the imaging criterion the denial turns on. Below I quote the plan's language and point to the specific record that matches it.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. The imaging criterion the denial relies on**

The plan's guideline states:

> "Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 6 months that correlates with clinical findings"

My MRI of the lumbar spine was performed on 2026-06-30 — within six months of the authorization request — and it documents an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. That is nerve root compression identified on advanced imaging, at a specific level and on a specific side.

The guideline also requires that imaging and clinical findings line up:

> "Imaging studies. All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

My records show that correlation. My symptoms are radicular pain into the right calf — the same side as the imaged compression. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The MRI report was read and reported by [name of the interpreting radiologist and facility, as shown on the MRI report of 2026-06-30]; I am asking that the radiologist's report be used, as the guideline provides.

The guideline also addresses radicular findings:

> "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:"

This sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of findings that was not reproduced in the policy text available to me. I am not going to guess at that list. My records document radicular pain into the right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit at the imaged level. If the plan applied a specific item from that list in denying my request, I ask that the plan identify it in writing.

**2. Conservative management**

The plan's guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

I completed supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility — 24 visits over 10 weeks, from 2026-04-10 to 2026-06-19. Alongside physical therapy, I took NSAIDs for four months with inadequate relief, and I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-14 that gave me only about three weeks of partial relief. That is physical therapy plus more than one additional conservative treatment.

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management (Physical therapy optional)"

My physical therapy alone ran 10 weeks, longer than the six weeks the guideline names, and my medication trial ran four months.

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My compliance is documented: 24 completed visits are recorded in the physical therapy discharge note, with the start and end dates above.

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

I completed that course and then some, and the surgery was requested only afterward.

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

My records describe nine months of progressive pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest, and I still cannot stand for more than 10 minutes. The injection helped for about three weeks and then the pain returned; the NSAIDs did not give adequate relief. I did not improve in any lasting way after a full course of conservative care.

**3. Pain and functional impairment**

The plan's guideline defines this term:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and that I have radicular pain into the right calf. For the specific items this criterion asks about, I refer the reviewer to [my documented pain rating as recorded in my office and physical therapy notes] and [the specific ADLs/IADLs I am unable to perform, as documented in my chart], and I ask that my treating records be requested if the plan needs them to complete this element.

**4. Other sources of pain**

> "All other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out"

I ask the plan to review [my surgeon's assessment addressing other potential sources of my pain, as documented in the office note] on this point. My records also note that I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

**5. Criteria I was not given in full**

Two of the plan's provisions available to me end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material I have:

> "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:"

> "Initial disc herniation when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

I am not going to speculate about what those lists contain. If any item on them was the basis for this denial, I ask the plan to tell me which one, so that I can respond to it directly. Apart from the passages I have quoted above, I have not been given the plan's full criteria, and no other policy language here is being attributed to the plan.

## Why I am asking for a different outcome

The denial rests on the imaging. The plan's own guideline asks for nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on advanced imaging performed within the past six months that correlates with clinical findings. My MRI of 2026-06-30 documents compression of the traversing L5 nerve root at L4-L5 with severe right lateral recess stenosis, and my examination findings — right-sided radicular pain into the calf, positive provocative testing on that side, and a neurologic deficit at the imaged level — are on the same side and at the same level. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me.

## What I am requesting

I respectfully ask that Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield (formerly Empire):

1. Overturn the denial of CPT 63030 and authorize the requested surgery;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with expertise in spine surgery;
3. If any part of the denial is upheld, identify in writing the specific criterion from *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon) that my records did not meet, and what documentation would satisfy it; and
4. Provide me with a copy of the complete criteria used in this review.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in my denial notice. The notice states my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-09**, and I am sending it to the appeal address printed on that denial letter. (Anthem/Elevance plans are state- and plan-specific; members can also log in at anthem.com or use the Sydney Health app, or call the number on the back of the ID card. The address on the denial letter is the authoritative one, and that is where I am sending this.)

Documents I am enclosing:
- Copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-13 (Reference POC-C3B5D8F398-85355)
- MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-06-30
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-10 to 2026-06-19, 24 visits)
- Office/operative planning notes from Lindqvist, MD
- [Any additional records I am including]

Thank you for taking a careful second look at this request. Please contact me at the phone number above if anything further is needed.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Sawyer Delgado**
Member ID: W188500611
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date signed]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy.
Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate.

For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs.

Imaging studies. All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure.
Acute neurologic deterioration including signs and symptoms of cauda equina syndrome, or rapid progression of neurologic deficits confirmed by imaging, regardless of underlying pathology.
Initial disc herniation when ALL of the following criteria are met:
Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 6 months that correlates with clinical findings
Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management (Physical therapy optional)
Recurrent disc herniation when BOTH criteria are met: • Requirements for initial herniation • Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management
Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care
Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation

The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when cauda equina syndrome or conus medullaris syndrome is present, and urgent intervention is indicated.
Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:
Progressive or severe neurologic deficits secondary to cauda equina, lateral recess or foraminal compression (conservative management requirement waived)
All other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out
